gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 concerns an invalid multiplicative quadrature comparison caused by finite collocation kernels, whereas the gold issue concerns the coefficient rescaling induced by the Monte Carlo representation and the resulting N-dependent regularizer. They are different formulas and failed obligations, despite both involving an empirical objective.

The gold issue is failure of empirical minimizer existence because negative quadrature weights make the objective unbounded below. ISSUE-005 diagnoses a separate false multiplicative relation between true and empirical losses; it neither identifies the sign hypothesis nor the resulting nonexistence of minimizers.

Both identify that finitely supported empirical measures cannot converge setwise to the relevant nonatomic target measure: the countable set of all collocation nodes has full empirical mass but zero target mass. Both therefore identify the failure of the stated measure-convergence premise and its effect on the convergence theorem.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The setwise convergence assumption is incompatible with finite-node quadrature approximating a nonatomic loss measure, making the advertised convergence chain inapplicable or vacuous for the intended regime.

component_coverage.gold_component: Setwise convergence of finitely supported empirical measures to an atomless target measure is impossible, so the intended finite-grid convergence regime is excluded.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 gives the same countable-union-of-collocation-points contradiction, identifies the resulting vacuity of the convergence result, and proposes replacing setwise convergence with a suitable weaker quadrature convergence notion.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false multiplicative comparison between the true loss and finite-collocation empirical loss. Both use the infinite-dimensional kernel of finite residual evaluations to show empirical loss can vanish while true loss is positive, and both replace the invalid multiplicative statement with a uniform additive quadrature estimate.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Finite residual evaluations have a nontrivial kernel in the infinite-dimensional trial space, so no uniform multiplicative bound L(v)≤C L-hat(v) can hold; the appropriate replacement is a uniform additive quadrature error bound.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed relative or multiplicative true-versus-empirical loss bound fails because finite collocation has a nonzero evaluation kernel, allowing zero empirical loss with positive true loss; the associated error-theorem proof therefore fails and requires an additive estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly states that quadrature errors are additive rather than multiplicative, constructs the finite-evaluation kernel counterexample, identifies the failure of the lemma and dependent theorem proof, and supplies the additive replacement and proof adjustment.
